text:
NICE NG148 (first published 2013 as CG169, updated 2019 and 2023) covers preventing, detecting and managing acute kidney injury in children, young people and adults, including critically ill patients. It remains the current UK national guideline.

DETECTION CRITERIA: Detect AKI in line with (p)RIFLE, AKIN or KDIGO definitions using any of: a rise in serum creatinine of 26 micromol/litre or greater within 48 hours; a 50% or greater rise in serum creatinine known or presumed to have occurred within the past 7 days; a fall in urine output to less than 0.5 ml/kg/hour for more than 6 hours in adults and more than 8 hours in children and young people; or a 25% or greater fall in eGFR in children and young people within the past 7 days. Monitor serum creatinine regularly in everyone with or at risk of AKI — daily measurement is typical while in hospital.

RISK ASSESSMENT AND PREVENTION: Assess AKI risk in acutely ill people, especially those with chronic kidney disease, heart failure, liver disease or diabetes. Review and where possible withhold nephrotoxic medicines. For adults receiving iodine-based contrast media, ensure adequate hydration and monitor creatinine afterwards. Maintain systems to recognize and respond to oliguria promptly.

IDENTIFYING THE CAUSE: Record the cause in the notes. Perform urine dipstick testing for blood, protein, leucocytes, nitrites and glucose as soon as AKI is suspected or detected. Consider acute nephritis with urgent nephrology referral when there is haematuria plus proteinuria with no obvious cause. Offer ultrasound of the urinary tract when pyonephrosis or obstruction is suspected.

MANAGEMENT AND REFERRAL: Relieve urological obstruction urgently. Discuss management with a nephrologist or paediatric nephrologist as soon as possible and within 24 hours of detection when there is a possible specialist diagnosis (vasculitis, glomerulonephritis, myeloma), no clear cause, inadequate response to treatment, AKI-related complications, stage 3 AKI, a renal transplant, or CKD stage 4-5. Refer immediately for renal replacement therapy when indicated. After an episode, monitor creatinine at a frequency based on stability of renal function, and consider nephrology follow-up if eGFR is 30 ml/min/1.73 m2 or less.
title: NICE NG148 — Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management
